stories.headline: The Download: AI’s gas power boom and a consciousness reality check
summary: Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants One of the biggest obstacles to building a data center is getting approval to connect to the grid, a wait that could last as long as a decade.
Some developers won’t wait and are instead building their own off-grid gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.
As of October 2026, developers had announced plans for more than 100 such gas power plants at data centers in the US.
But bypassing the grid brings its own problems, from worsening climate emissions to potentially higher energy bills for everyone else.
This was reported by MIT Technology Review; the original article has the full details and is linked below.
stories.whyItMatters: New AI models often end up inside the everyday apps and tools people already use, so their abilities set what's possible next.

stories.headline: Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
summary: One of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade.

Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom. xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024.
At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators.
It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles .
This was reported by MIT Technology Review; the original article has the full details and is linked below.
stories.whyItMatters: Rules like this shape what AI companies are allowed to do, and how much protection and transparency the public gets.

stories.headline: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
summary: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features.

The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI "in ways that may not be apparent to users." In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads , two of the Times ' photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features "can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated." Adobe has spent the past few years filling Photoshop and other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools.

stories.whyItMatters: Tools like this change what ordinary people and workers can do with AI day to day, often without needing any technical skill.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
summary: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg , The New York Times , and The Handbasket's Marisa Kabas .

During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement - an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself - "completely untrue." He added, "Don't think for a second politics played a role in the company.
We are the most apolitical company," according to Kabas .
This was reported by The Verge; the original article has the full details and is linked below.
stories.whyItMatters: Changes like this can affect jobs, hiring, and how companies operate, which matters even if you don't work in tech.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop
summary: Jensen Huang is partying it up in Ibiza.
In a video with nearly 6 million views on Instagram, the former CEO of Nvidia is dancing in a crowded club, champagne glass in hand, still wearing his signature black leather jacket.

Suddenly, from behind him, Alice Huang - the Chinese technology executive and suspected spy he had an affair with , sparking congressional investigations and his resignation from the chipmaking company he cofounded - appears.
She puts her hand on his shoulder and he wraps his arm around her waist as they begin dancing together.
This was reported by The Verge; the original article has the full details and is linked below.
stories.whyItMatters: Moves by major AI companies shape which tools get built, funded, and widely adopted next.
